newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S. Africa's Zuma backs down over drug reforms.
newsitem.headline: S. Africa's Zuma backs down over drug reforms.

text.p: The South African government on Thursday backed down over proposed healthcare reforms by withdrawing a key regulation that had seen drugs firm SmithKline Beecham Plc challenge it in court.
The Anglo-American drugs firm took legal action to scrap plans which would have made prescribing generic drugs mandatory and limited the dispensing of medicines.
The firm filed a submission asking the Supreme Court's Transvaal Division to fight the regulation, which is part of an overall reform programme for healthcare in South Africa.
Late on Thursday the health ministry issued a statement saying the regulation had been withdrawn due to a huge response from industry and the public.

"As a result of that overwhelming response I have directed the department to withdraw regulation number R1150 and to prepare new draft regulations which will take into account some of the comments received," the statement from Zuma said.
The plans had caused outrage in the South African drugs industry.
Generic drugs are cheaper versions of money-spinning branded products that have come off patent.
Despite the backdown the ministry still plans to act tough with the sector. "The principles in those (withdrawn) regulations will still stand," the statement said.
Drug industry figures welcomed the news and struck a conciliatory tone.
"The industry and private health care sector look forward to working in a constructive dialogue and true partnership with government," said SmithKline South Africa chief executive Gunter Faber.
The ongoing dispute between the ministry and the drug industry has stoked fears foreign drug firms may disinvest from South Africa.
With the regulations now withdrawn that prospect looks set to dim.
